news.title: US to host first Women's Club World Cup in 2028
news.lede: The US is also set to co-host the Women's World Cup in 2031. The United States will host the inaugural Women's Club World Cup in January 2028, Fifa has confirmed. Arsenal have been named as one of seven teams set to play in the tournament, with a further 12 clubs to be determined at a later date. The 19-team tournament, designed to echo the revamped men's Club World Cup and take place every four years, is scheduled from 5-30 January 2028.

news.title: United States to Host First FIFA Women’s Club World Cup in 2028
news.lede: Casablanca - FIFA has chosen the United States to host the inaugural Women's Club World Cup, which will bring together 19 clubs from six continental confederations between January 5 and 30, 2028. The decision, announced on Thursday by the Bureau of the FIFA Council, gives the US another major international football competition following the expanded men's Club World Cup in 2025 and the 2026 FIFA World Cup, which it co-hosted with Mexico and Canada. The tournament will take place every four years and offer women's clubs an opportunity to compete for a world title. FIFA's Chief Women's Football Officer, Sarai Bareman, explained that the governing body selected the US after evaluating potential hosts.

news.title: Fifa increases preparation money for Women’s World Cup to match men’s teams
news.lede: Funds for 2027 will match men’s World Cup in 2026. Players given better flights and individual hotel rooms. Teams in the 2027’s Women’s World Cup in Brazil will receive the same preparation money from Fifa as those that played at the 2026 men’s tournament, the world’s governing body has announced. The preparation money for the 32 teams has been more than doubled to $2.5m (£1.86m) each.

news.title: FIFA Approves $2.5m Preparation Fund for Women’s World Cup Teams, Names USA 2028 Club World Cup Host
news.lede: The Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA) has approved a new financial distribution model for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup, increasing preparation funding for participating countries to $2.5 million per team while committing to improved support for players. The decision was among several major resolutions reached by the Bureau of the FIFA Council following the Council’s meeting in Zurich, Switzerland, on October 15, 2026. Under the approved framework, funding for the women’s tournament in Brazil in 2027 will comprise prize money, preparation funding and allocations through FIFA’s Club Benefits Programme. The move is expected to strengthen preparations for the competition and provide participating member associations with additional resources to support their teams ahead of the global tournament.

news.title: FIFA World Cup media rights — Tender process begins for USA-Puerto rights WC 2030 and 2034
news.lede: Reuters Reuters https://ss-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/itjnm0/article71613141.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/Spain%20World%20Cup.jpg FIFA is looking for a broadcaster for the next two World Cups who can reach large audiences through new approaches, with the bid submission deadline set on November 19. Chennai FIFA has opened the tender process for the media rights of the 2030 FIFA World Cup and a further option to secure the 2034 edition. This is exclusively for the United States and Puerto Rico. On Thursday, FIFA said in a press release, it is looking for a broadcaster that can reach large audiences through innovative approaches as well as be able to contribute revenues to the benefit of football, with the deadline for submission of bids set on November 19.

news.title: USA to host women's football Club World Cup in 2028 - FIFA
news.lede: Paris (France) (AFP) – The United States will host the inaugural women's football Club World Cup in 2028, FIFA announced Thursday. "The decision was taken in view of its experience in organising FIFA tournaments, the maturity of its infrastructure and services and the level of stakeholder interest in women's football in the country," world football's governing body said. The US has a proven track record of staging large sporting events, notably co-hosting the men's World Cup earlier this year. The first-ever women's Club World Cup will be staged from January 5-30, 2028.
